title: An adjustable label keeps a name that still makes sense once you change it
goal: When you make one word of your component adjustable, the knob takes that word as its name. So a button that says Save gets a knob called Save, and the moment a copy says Cancel instead the panel reads Save then Cancel, which looks like a mistake. The knob should be named for what it controls, not for what it currently says.
notes: Found in the step E9 sitting on 2026-09-03, see queue/audits/2026-09-03-component-e2e-4-overridden.png. The five starter components dodge this by shipping the knob pre-named Label; only hand authored components hit it. Naming lives in ComponentProperties.swift / the Adjustable list in ComponentPanel.swift. The current rule is documented in docs/design/ui-building.md under the C6 landing note, so change that too.
acceptance: Making the words of a text layer adjustable gives the knob a name that does not change meaning when a copy overrides it
An existing document with knobs named after their words keeps working and is not renamed behind the user back
The name is still a field you can type your own name into
A picture in the audit shows a copy whose override reads sensibly next to its knob name
